question: Find the simple interest (in ₹) on ₹900 at an interest rate of 6% per month in 12 months.
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Total interest percentage for **12 months** = 6% × 12 = 72%

**Simple Interest** = 72% of **Principal**

SI = 72% of 900 = 72 × 9 = 648

**∴ The correct answer is ₹648.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f9c064585d330b74d43399b3c3aa3971a7ed39e8e533940d58219ba8604a17a.png] 

**Given:**

**Principal (P)** = ₹900

**Rate of interest (R)** = 6% per month

**Time period (T)** = 12 months

**Formula Used:**

Simple Interest (SI) = (P × R × T) ÷ 100

**Calculations:**

⇒ SI = (900 × 6 × 12) ÷ 100

⇒ SI = 9 × 6 × 12

⇒ SI = 54 × 12

⇒ SI = 648

**∴ The correct answer is ₹648.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Total Amount Formula

The total **Amount (A)** after the interest period is the sum of the **Principal** and the **Simple Interest**: A = P + SI.

Unit Consistency Rule

Always ensure that the **Rate (R)** and **Time (T)** are in the same unit (e.g., both monthly or both annual) before applying the formula.

Simple Interest vs Compound Interest

In **Simple Interest**, interest is calculated only on the initial principal, whereas in **Compound Interest**, interest is calculated on the principal plus the accumulated interest of previous periods.
